title: Daily X narrative digest — 2026-09-28

hits.name: Alex Finn
hits.text:
This is bigger news than it appears

I’ve had early access to Sonnet 5.5 for a bit now and honestly at first I couldn’t tell the difference between this and Opus 5.5

It’s a fraction of the price of Opus, which already felt like you got an absurd amounts of usage out of for cheap

It’s clear Anthropic has had some sort of breakthrough the last month

The jump in intelligence, speed, and affordability of all their 5.5 models is maybe the biggest leap we’ve ever seen in AI

You need to be using this model for all your standard, fastball down the center work

With its speed and intelligence you’ll be shocked at how fast you get tasks done

Introducing Claude Sonnet 5.5, the second model in the Claude 5.5 family.

It’s a clear upgrade over Sonnet 5, runs more than 30% faster, and costs up to 30% less for most work.
hits.hook: This is bigger news than it appears
hits.draft_en:
The quiet model that matches the expensive one is the real product launch.

Alex has early Sonnet 5.5 access and could not tell it apart from Opus 5.5 at a fraction of the price. That is not a nice upgrade. That is the mid-tier eating the frontier for daily work.

If you still route every task to the max model, you are buying ego, not throughput.

Put Sonnet-class models on the fastball work. Keep the heavy model for the 10% that actually needs it. Track tokens per shipped feature.

Switch the default today. Speed plus price is the new IQ.
hits.video_tip: 10-12s: price tags Opus vs Sonnet, same output scroll, caption mid-tier ate the frontier.

hits.name: Pieter Levels
hits.text:
I think every time AI can do something equally good or better than humans it stops being valuable or special

Marketing videos used to take lots of work of editing and motion graphics and a big budget 

Now with Opus 5.5 etc it costs $0 to make one as good or better

That means ANYONE can make a marketing video now, so the timeline gets flooded with these videos (as you see happening now) and people stop caring about them, stop watching them and they stop grabbing attention

The response then to still grab attention is be different and that probably means IRL marketing videos that are original and unique and maybe personal

It's the grim reaper meme where AI keeps commoditizing another media format and bringing the cost down to close to $0

It already did so for graphic design (2023), last year with Nano Banana for photography (2025), this year with Seedance 2.5 it did it for video (2026) and this and next year motion graphics

hot take i’ve been mulling over:

launch videos are dead (or at least in their dying breath)

oh people will still do them but they are a dying form, actual good, valuable launches will pivot to different forms
hits.hook: I think every time AI can do something equally good or better than humans it stops being valuable or special
hits.draft_en:
When AI matches human quality, the craft stops being the moat. Distribution and taste take the seat.

Levels: Opus makes marketing videos for near $0, timelines flood, attention dies, and the survivors go IRL and personal.

Launch videos are in their dying breath. The scarce thing is not can we render it. It is who trusts it and buys.

If your edge was polish, you got commoditized. If your edge is audience and iteration speed, you got a free factory.

Ship 10 weird variants. Kill 9. Put budget into distribution, not the next Seedance pass.
hits.video_tip: 9-12s: $0 AI render flood vs one IRL personal clip, end card moat = distribution.

hits.name: Alex Finn
hits.text:
OpenAI just announced that the $200 subscription will get half the amount of usage moving forward

It’s clear where all of this is going

All AI companies within the next 2 years will exclusively use API pricing. No more subscriptions

Subs only made sense when companies were willing to lose billions of dollars to get you into their ecosystem

Now that basically every AI company will be attempting to go public, they’ll no longer be able to burn extraordinary amounts of money

They’ll have to report their earnings to the street, and if the number isn’t going up and to the right, that’ll be really bad

I don’t think this is doomsday. The cheaper models like Luna and Sonnet are now actually really good. Compared to 6 months ago, they’d actually be frontier

That’s more than enough to be spectacularly productive for a good price

The consumer behavior is going to have to change. You are going to need to be fine with using an intelligence level appropriate for your work. Not just Astra 6 Max for every single thing you do

If you have a Ferrari and a Model 3 in your driveway, you don’t drive the Ferrari to pick up milk from 7/11. Sometimes you use the daily driver car

The days of AI subsidies are coming to an end, and it’s probably time we start getting used to it. The party is over.

Hi,

Tomorrow we are re-opening the Pro $200 subscriptions to new subscribers, but together with it we are also changing how we calculate the usage for it. In effect, if you do the math, it will net out at half the dollar in API spend compared to the old Pro $200 plan. 

Now that
hits.hook: OpenAI just announced that the $200 subscription will get half the amount of usage moving forward
hits.draft_en:
The $200 AI buffet is shrinking. API metering is the endgame.

OpenAI is cutting Pro usage roughly in half. Alex's read: within two years, flat subscriptions lose to API pricing because public companies cannot keep subsidizing tokens forever.

That is not doomsday. Cheaper models are now good enough that last year's frontier is today's daily driver.

Stop treating every prompt like a Ferrari errand. Match intelligence to the job. Budget tokens like AWS, not Netflix.

Audit your last 100 calls. Route 80% to the cheap model. Keep the expensive brain for the hard 20%.
hits.video_tip: 11-14s: buffet plate halved, API meter spinning, caption party over / meter on.

hits.name: Pieter Levels
hits.text:
Lindt has an active lawsuit going against it for elevated levels of lead and cadmium

Most interestingly Lindt's lawyers themselves have suggested Lindt is not "expertly crafted" or "excellent" but that that is just advertising

So if even Lindt itself doesn't consider itself good, why should I be eating Lindt chocolate?

Now I eat Vivani which sources from Panama which seems cleaner chocolate beans

Lindt is the worst chocolate in Switzerland. Hard no go for me. x.com/blickch/status…
hits.hook: Lindt has an active lawsuit going against it for elevated levels of lead and cadmium
hits.draft_en:
When a brand's own lawyers walk back expertly crafted, trust is the product and the product is on trial.

Levels posted Lindt's lead/cadmium suit and the lawyers undercutting the excellence claim. Receipts beat slogans.

Builders can steal the structure. Find the gap between the marketing line and the legal footnote. Post the contrast with sources.

If you sell AI-powered excellence, assume someone will screenshot your disclaimer.

Ship receipts. Soft claims die in court and on timelines.
hits.video_tip: 8-11s: glossy ad claim hard cut to lawsuit PDF highlight, post the receipt.

hits.name: Tony Dinh
hits.text: You can do this on your own now. So cool.
hits.hook: You can do this on your own now. So cool.
hits.draft_en:
The unlock is not the tool drop. It is the sentence: you can do this on your own now.

Tony's short line travels because it hands agency back. No agency. No waitlist story. Just capability transferred.

For AI tools content, compress the demo into one proof the reader can repeat tonight.

If your post needs a 12-step funnel before the aha, you buried the product.

Show the before/after. End with you can run this tonight.
hits.video_tip: 6-9s: screen record one-click result, big caption you can do this on your own now.

hits.name: Greg Isenberg
hits.text:
It's kind of wild how many new primitives AI has given us in 3 years:

- Local models (2023: Llama, Ollama, LM Studio)
- Voice cloning (2023: ElevenLabs)
- Text to CAD (2023: Zoo)
- Text to video (2024: Sora, Veo, Runway)
- Real-time voice (2024: Gemini Live, ChatGPT Voice)
- Memory (2024: ChatGPT)
- Reasoning models (2024: OpenAI o1, DeepSeek R1)
- Vibe coding (2024: Bolt, Lovable, v0)
- Computer use (2024: Claude, OpenAI Operator)
- Connectors (2024: MCP)
- Deep research (2024: Gemini, Perplexity, OpenAI Deep Research)
- Agents (2025: Claude Code, Codex, Manus)
- Image editing (2025: GPT-4o images, Nano Banana)
- Agent payments (2025: x402, AP2)
- Skills (2025: Claude Skills)
- Personal agents (2026: Grokbot, Muse, Instinct)... we are here now.

Each one of these is a starting point for hundreds of companies.

The most interesting ones I'm seeing combine 2 or 3 of them with a specific niche!
hits.hook: It's kind of wild how many new primitives AI has given us in 3 years:
hits.draft_en:
Three years of AI primitives is a menu, not a museum. The money is in combining two or three inside a niche.

Greg lists the stack from local models to personal agents. Each line is a company seed. The interesting builds mash connectors + agents + payments for one vertical.

Stop collecting demos. Pick two primitives and one painful workflow.

If your roadmap is another wrapper on a single API, you are late to the menu.

Write the combo on a sticky note. Ship the niche glue this week.
hits.video_tip: 12-15s: cascading primitive chips stacking into one niche product, caption combine 2-3.

hits.draft_en:
50k installs and then a quiet rebuild is the grown-up SaaS arc.

Hassan on Hallmark v2 after months of feedback. Not a launch scream. A listen-and-rebuild loop.

Distribution without product listening is a leaky bucket. Product listening without a ship date is a diary.

If you have early users, the next post should be what you killed, not what you added.

List three pieces of feedback. Ship the v2 wedge. Date the drop.
hits.video_tip: 9-12s: install counter 50k to rebuild montage, caption listen then v2.

virals.name: aslam
virals.text: What’s the biggest problem with AI coding tools right now?
virals.hook: What’s the biggest problem with AI coding tools right now?

virals_narrative: Last ~48h outsider heat: Opus 5.5 motion-design launch videos going nuclear, staff-replacement AI tooling confessions, Amex GBT $6.3B close, OpenRouter Opus 5.5 week-one check-in, singularity-style multi-product launch day hype, plus watchlist pressure from Sonnet 5.5 mid-tier leap and OpenAI Pro usage cuts.
narrative_synthesis: Last ~48h outsider heat: Opus 5.5 motion-design launch videos going nuclear, staff-replacement AI tooling confessions, Amex GBT $6.3B close, OpenRouter Opus 5.5 week-one check-in, singularity-style multi-product launch day hype, plus watchlist pressure from Sonnet 5.5 mid-tier leap and OpenAI Pro usage cuts.
patterns: Mid-tier models eating frontier for daily work (Sonnet 5.5 ~ Opus feel, fraction of price)
AI subscription buffet ending → API metering / half usage on $200 Pro
When AI matches craft, moat moves to distribution + IRL/personal (launch videos dying)
Receipts vs slogans (Lindt lawyers walk back excellence)
Agency handoff one-liners: you can do this on your own now
$5T AI roll-up / one-person holdco with agents (map + folders + objections)
AI primitives menu: combine 2-3 in a niche (local → personal agents)
Scene posts from the room (Dev Day rooftop) beat press-release voice
Short meme/UI callouts timed to product moments (oai designers trolling)

drafts.inspired_by: @alexfinn Sonnet 5.5 ≈ Opus at fraction of price
drafts.draft_en:
Stop defaulting every task to the most expensive model.

Sonnet-class 5.5 is landing close enough to Opus that the gap is ego, not output. Same work. Fraction of the bill. Faster loop.

If your agent stack still burns max tokens for CRUD and copy edits, you are funding someone else's earnings call.

Set a routing rule tonight: cheap model first, escalate only on failure.

Measure tokens per shipped feature, not vibes per prompt.
drafts.video_tip: 10-12s: router animation cheap→escalate, caption ego is not a model picker.

drafts.draft_en:
The AI buffet is closing. Metered API is the adult form of this market.

When flat $200 plans get halved, it is not a gotcha. It is the IPO diet. Subsidies do not survive the street.

Good news: last year's frontier models are this year's daily drivers. You do not need a Ferrari to pick up milk.

Rebuild your stack around job-sized intelligence. Budget tokens like cloud spend.

Cut one max-model habit this week. Put the savings into distribution.
drafts.video_tip: 9-11s: buffet lid slam to API meter, caption subsidies end / ship on a budget.

drafts.draft_en:
Launch videos are becoming background noise because everyone can render one for free.

When craft hits $0, attention flees polished sameness and pays for weird, personal, IRL proof.

If your GTM is another Seedance hero clip, you are competing with infinite twins.

Swap one polished render for a sweaty screen recording of the product making money.

Ship the ugly proof. Spend the production budget on distribution.

drafts.draft_en:
The AI primitives menu is long. The businesses are short: two primitives plus one niche.

Local models, connectors, agents, payments, memory. Each line is a seed. The winners glue two or three onto a painful workflow nobody else owns.

Wrappers on a single API are late. Glue with a customer is early.

Pick one niche headache. Attach an agent and a connector. Charge for the outcome.

Write the combo on a sticky note. Ship the glue this week.

drafts.draft_en:
You do not need a holdco fantasy to steal the operator file tree.

Greg's $5T roll-up episode works because it hands over folders, agent files, and the counterarguments. Thesis plus ops plus objections.

Indie builders can run a baby version: one cashflow loop, agents as staff, kill criteria on paper.

If you cannot name the folders, you are collecting podcasts, not running a shop.

Draft your one-person SOP today. Put an agent on the boring loop first.
drafts.video_tip: 12-15s: folder tree + agent avatars as staff, caption SOP before scale fantasy.
